title: Impact of idiopathic short stature on children's well-being: a nationwide study of short Danish children.
abstract: It remains unclear whether idiopathic short stature (ISS), defined as a height below -2.0 SD score (SDS) without an identifiable cause, adversely affects psychosocial well-being. To assess the psychosocial impact of ISS in children using nationwide registry and survey data. The nationwide cohort study included children identified between 2012 and 2020. The final cohort included 16121 children with ISS. Each child was matched to 5 controls by age, sex, and region. Children with ISS had higher odds of feeling bullied, lonely, and insecure. Children with ISS displayed increased psychosocial distress. These findings support psychosocial assessment in children with ISS to enable timely intervention.

title: Placental gene signatures associated with high neonatal adiposity: role for immune cell activation.
abstract: Fetal fat accumulation is an important indicator of the nutritional environment in pregnancy and placental function. Excessive fat accretion leading to high adiposity at birth can increase a child's long-term risk for obesity and metabolic disease. We profiled the transcriptomics of 79 placentas collected from mothers with and without obesity. We identified a set of 18 neonatal adiposity-associated genes. These findings suggest that placental inflammation may influence fetal fat accumulation.

title: A prospective cohort study of the factors associated with recurrence in young patients with thyroid cancer.
abstract: The incidence of thyroid cancer in young people has increased over the past 40 years. While prognosis is favorable, recurrence rates may reach 20%. To identify predictors of recurrence in pediatric and adolescent thyroid cancer. A prospective cohort of 213 patients aged 5-19 years who underwent initial surgery between 2012 and 2020. Seventeen of 213 patients (8.0%) experienced recurrence during a median follow-up of 8 years. Younger age was the strongest predictor of recurrence. Unilateral lobectomy was not associated with an increased risk of recurrence. These findings provide clinically relevant prognostic insights that may help refine clinical management in young patients with thyroid cancer.

title: A worldwide perspective on clinical characteristics and treatment of youth with monogenic diabetes in the SWEET registry.
abstract: To characterize youth with monogenic diabetes worldwide in the SWEET database and define trends in clinical care and outcomes. Youth with monogenic diabetes between the ages of 0 and 21 years from 44 worldwide centers in the SWEET registry. This included 690 youth. Globally, mean age and hemoglobin A1c at diagnosis were 10.1 years and 6.9%. At diabetes diagnosis, 3.6% presented in diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA). Worldwide, patients with monogenic diabetes typically present during late childhood/early adolescence with mild elevation in HbA1c, normal BMI, and lack of DKA. Regional differences in demographics and treatment modalities highlight heterogeneity in presentation and management of monogenic diabetes.

title: Free testosterone independently predicts metabolic syndrome severity in U.S. adolescent girls aged 12-19 years.
abstract: Hyperandrogenemia is associated with increased risks for metabolic syndrome in asymptomatic women and women with polycystic ovary syndrome. The aim was to assess whether free testosterone concentrations predict metabolic syndrome severity (MSS) in adolescent girls. Using data from the U.S. National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (2013-2016), we performed weighted regression analysis. 287 girls aged 12-19 years. Higher free testosterone predicts greater MSS in a nationally representative sample of adolescent girls aged 12-19 years.

title: Comprehensive genetic rescreening improves diagnostic yield in congenital hyperinsulinism.
abstract: Recent genetic discoveries in congenital hyperinsulinism (HI) and advances in sequencing technology suggest that the diagnostic yield may be improved by rescreening in people with genetically unsolved HI. Twenty-seven probands underwent rescreening targeting the coding regions of 18 known HI genes. Genetic rescreening was informative in 22% of cases. Definitive genetic diagnoses were established in 4 participants. These findings emphasize the importance of regularly updating genetic testing strategies in genetically unexplained HI cases.

title: Burosumab treatment in an adult with FGF23-mediated hypophosphatemia due to cutaneous skeletal hypophosphatemia syndrome.
abstract: Cutaneous skeletal hypophosphatemia syndrome (CSHS) is an ultrarare disorder defined by epidermal and/or melanocytic nevi, mosaic skeletal dysplasia, and FGF23-mediated hypophosphatemia. Burosumab is a fully human immunoglobulin G1 monoclonal antibody that binds to and inhibits the activity of FGF23. In this open-label, single-patient trial, burosumab was administered subcutaneously every 4 weeks for 3 years to an 18-year-old woman with CSHS. Burosumab therapy was well tolerated with correction of hypophosphatemia. These findings suggest that burosumab may be an effective treatment for CSHS.

title: Impact of antenatal exposure to a mixture of endocrine disruptors on attentional and executive functions in children.
abstract: Numerous studies indicate negative associations between early life exposure to endocrine-disrupting chemicals and various aspects of neurodevelopment. Two polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) and 4 perfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) were measured in the cord blood from 55 children. At 6 years of age, attentional and executive functions were assessed. These results support associations between antenatal exposure to a mixture of endocrine disruptors and attention and executive development, emphasizing a sex-specific effect.

title: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances and adolescent bone mineral density: assessing periods of susceptibility.
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) may affect adolescent bone mineral density (BMD), but few studies have examined periods of susceptibility. Among 218 children in a prospective pregnancy and birth cohort, we quantified serum concentrations of PFAS. We measured BMD at 6 skeletal sites using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry at age 12 years. Serum PFOA concentrations from delivery to age 12 years were associated with lower 1/3 distal radius bone mineral density in early adolescence.

title: Adipose tissue distribution and metabolic profile of young individuals with turner syndrome.
abstract: Turner syndrome (TS) is the most common sex chromosome abnormality in females. Incidence of cardiometabolic complications is high in TS. Obesity and high visceral adiposity are additional risk factors. This is a cross-sectional study. Twenty-seven TS, 15 obese, and 15 lean youth were recruited (13-19 years; female). Visceral adiposity and fat mass from DXA were higher for the TS group. The prevalence of dyslipidemia was 38% in the TS group. Bioelectrical impedance may be a convenient noninvasive outpatient tool in TS to assess body composition.

title: The ontogeny of sex differences in exercise performance.
abstract: Sex differences in adult athletic performance are driven by the increase in testosterone production of male puberty creating larger and stronger muscle, bone and cardiorespiratory functions. Before puberty, boys also surpass girls in age-group records despite no difference in circulating testosterone. This was a secondary analysis of exercise performance of 85347 healthy 9- to 17-year-old Australian schoolchildren. These findings confirm that the quantitatively dominant sex differences in exercise performance are those of puberty.

title: Androgen and estrogen secretory dynamics in longitudinally followed moderately and late preterm infant girls.
abstract: Mini-puberty is a period when the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis is activated and is believed to create the basis for future fertility. To study sex steroid secretory dynamics in girls born moderately to late preterm during infancy. From a population-based longitudinal cohort of 70 girls born at gestational age 32.0 to 36.9 weeks, androgen and estrogen concentrations were analyzed during infancy with high-sensitivity mass spectrometry. In girls born moderately to late preterm, DHT, estradiol, and testosterone show postnatal activity. Degree of prematurity but not birth weight influences sex steroid secretion.
